slides.title: An animated logo is [not a motion identity].
slides.lede: Motion branding is a system of rules for how your brand moves, and for when it should stay still.

slides.title: Remove the logo. [Would clients still know you?]
slides.text: If typography, pacing, composition and transitions don't identify the firm, the work may be energetic, but it is not yet branded.

items.title: Timing
items.text: A controlled pace for each kind of movement.

items.title: Easing
items.text: Shapes perceived personality more than direction.

items.title: Directionality
items.text: A signature path that reinforces reading flow.

items.title: Scale and hierarchy
items.text: What moves first, and what stays fixed.

items.title: Interruption
items.text: Never make people wait for an animation.

items.title: Stillness
items.text: No movement for disclosures or dense figures.

slides.title: Approve motion where people [actually see it]
slides.note: A hero animation can pass review and **still fail on the website, social or PowerPoint.**

slides.title: Design [reduced motion] in from the start

cards.label: Full motion
cards.text: Slide-in transitions, parallax and looping backgrounds.

cards.label: Reduced motion
cards.text: Immediate appearance, static layers and a loop that pauses.

slides.quote: Attention alone is not a business outcome.
slides.text: Judge each asset by its objective: comprehension, qualified enquiries, template adoption or task completion.

slides.title: Build a system, [not just an animated logo].
slides.lede: Motion branding for B2B firms. Read the full guide via the link in our bio.
